categories.name: Evidence of impact
categories.intro: Does the product actually improve learning, and how do they know?

categories.name: Data privacy
categories.intro: What happens to student and staff data, during the contract and after it ends?

categories.name: Bias and accessibility
categories.intro: Does it work fairly and fully for all of our students, including those it was least tested on?

categories.name: Cost and exit terms
categories.intro: What will this really cost over time, and can we leave cleanly?

categories.name: Classroom fit
categories.intro: Will teachers actually use it, and will it support learning rather than replace it?

questions.question: What specific student outcome did your research measure, and how was it measured?
questions.why_it_matters: "Improves learning" can mean test scores, engagement, time on the platform, or teacher satisfaction. Only some of those are learning.
questions.weak_answer: Usage numbers, engagement rates, or satisfaction surveys presented as if they were learning gains.

questions.question: Who funded the research, and who conducted it?
questions.why_it_matters: Company-funded studies aren't automatically wrong, but they need more scrutiny, and you deserve to know who paid.
questions.weak_answer: "Independent researchers" with no names, or a study run entirely by the company's own team without saying so.

questions.question: Did the study compare students who used the product with similar students who didn't? How were they chosen?
questions.why_it_matters: Without a comparison group, gains could come from normal growth, a new teacher, or anything else that happened that year.
questions.weak_answer: Pre/post results with no comparison, or comparisons where schools chose for themselves whether to participate.

questions.question: How large was the effect, and for which students?
questions.why_it_matters: A result can be statistically significant and still too small to matter, or it may hold only for one group of students.
questions.weak_answer: "Statistically significant" with no effect size, or results reported only for the highest-using students.

questions.question: Which version of the product was studied, and how different is it from what we would buy today?
questions.why_it_matters: AI products change quickly, including the models underneath them. Evidence about last year's version may not describe this year's.
questions.weak_answer: A study of an older version or a different underlying model, presented as evidence for the current product.

questions.question: When you say the product is "research-based," do you mean research on this product, or research on the ideas behind it?
questions.why_it_matters: Citing general learning science (like retrieval practice) is not evidence that this particular product works.
questions.weak_answer: A list of well-known learning science studies, none of which tested the product itself.

questions.question: Has the evidence been reviewed or published outside your company? If you claim an ESSA evidence tier, who determined it?
questions.why_it_matters: Vendors often assign their own evidence tier. Outside review and a clear source for the claim make it far more credible.
questions.weak_answer: A white paper hosted only on the company website, or an ESSA tier the company assigned to itself.

questions.question: What results have you found that were neutral or negative?
questions.why_it_matters: Studies that find no effect are often never shared. A vendor who discusses them is giving you a more complete picture.
questions.weak_answer: "None." Every product has some setting, group, or measure where it didn't help.

questions.question: How much use did students need to see results, and how often did schools actually reach that level?
questions.why_it_matters: If results require 90 minutes a week and most schools average 20, the evidence may not apply to how you'd really use it.
questions.weak_answer: Results reported only for students who met the recommended usage, with no information on how many did.

questions.question: How is the AI's output checked for accuracy before students or teachers rely on it, and what is its known error rate?
questions.why_it_matters: AI tools can produce confident, wrong content. You need to know how often that happens and who catches it.
questions.weak_answer: "Our model is highly accurate" with no error rate, testing process, or description of human review.

questions.question: What student and staff data do you collect, and what is each type used for?
questions.why_it_matters: You can't judge risk without a specific list. Collecting more than the product needs increases exposure.
questions.weak_answer: "Only what's necessary" without an actual list of data fields and purposes.

questions.question: Is any of our data used to train or improve AI models, yours or a third party's?
questions.why_it_matters: Data used for training can be hard or impossible to remove later. This should be an explicit yes or no in the contract.
questions.weak_answer: "De-identified data may be used to improve our services," with no detail on what that includes.

questions.question: Which outside companies, including AI model providers, receive our data, and under what terms?
questions.why_it_matters: Many AI tools send data to another company's model. Your data is only as protected as the weakest company it passes through.
questions.weak_answer: "Trusted partners" with no names, or no mention of the model provider at all.

questions.question: How long do you keep our data, and how is it deleted when the contract ends?
questions.why_it_matters: Data kept indefinitely is a long-term risk. You want a timeline and written confirmation of deletion.
questions.weak_answer: No retention timeline, or deletion only "upon request" with no confirmation.

questions.question: Will you sign our state or district student data privacy agreement?
questions.why_it_matters: Many states and districts use standard agreements, often through the Student Data Privacy Consortium. Willingness to sign one is a basic signal.
questions.weak_answer: Only the company's own terms of service, or a refusal to negotiate any changes.

questions.question: How does the product handle students under 13, and what consent does it rely on?
questions.why_it_matters: Federal law (COPPA) sets rules for collecting data from children under 13. Ask your district's legal or privacy staff how it applies to you.
questions.weak_answer: An assumption that the school has handled consent, with no explanation of what the product collects from young students.

questions.question: What happens to our data if your company is acquired, merges, or shuts down?
questions.why_it_matters: Edtech companies are bought and closed often. The contract should say what happens to your data when that happens.
questions.weak_answer: Not addressed in the contract, or "we'd handle that at the time."

questions.question: Was the product tested with students like ours, including English learners, students with disabilities, and students from different backgrounds?
questions.why_it_matters: A tool tested on a narrow group of students may work worse for others, and you won't know unless you ask.
questions.weak_answer: "It works for all students," with no results broken out by student group.

questions.question: Does the AI perform differently for different groups of students, and how do you check?
questions.why_it_matters: AI scoring and feedback can be less accurate for some students. Vendors who monitor this can show you how.
questions.weak_answer: "Our model is unbiased," with no description of how that was tested or monitored.

questions.question: How does the AI handle student writing or speech in different dialects, varieties of English, or other languages?
questions.why_it_matters: Speech recognition and writing feedback can penalize students for how they speak or write rather than what they know.
questions.weak_answer: Testing only on standard academic English, or no answer about multilingual students.

questions.question: Can you share a current accessibility conformance report (such as a VPAT) showing which accessibility standards the product meets?
questions.why_it_matters: Schools are responsible for making digital tools usable by students with disabilities. A recent, specific report shows the vendor has actually checked.
questions.weak_answer: "Fully accessible," with no report, or a report several versions old.

questions.question: Can students who use screen readers, keyboard-only navigation, or other assistive technology use every feature, including the AI features?
questions.why_it_matters: New AI features are often added after accessibility testing was done on the rest of the product.
questions.weak_answer: The core product was tested, but the AI chat or newer features were not.

questions.question: What content does the AI refuse or filter, and who decided those rules?
questions.why_it_matters: Filters can block legitimate topics in history or health, or let inappropriate content through. You should know the rules before students do.
questions.weak_answer: "We use industry-standard filters," with no explanation of what is blocked or allowed.

questions.question: When the AI makes a judgment about a student, such as a score, flag, or recommendation, can a teacher see why and override it?
questions.why_it_matters: Decisions that affect students need a person who can explain them to the student and family, and change them when they're wrong.
questions.weak_answer: A score or flag with no explanation, and no way for a teacher to correct it.

questions.question: When the AI gets something wrong about a student, how is the record corrected?
questions.why_it_matters: Wrong information that stays in a student's record can follow them. There should be a clear correction process.
questions.weak_answer: No correction process, or corrections that only change what the teacher sees.

questions.question: What is the full cost over three years, including training, integrations, and expected price increases?
questions.why_it_matters: First-year pricing is often discounted. The real decision depends on the full cost over the life of the contract.
questions.weak_answer: A first-year price only, or "introductory pricing" with no figures for later years.

questions.question: Which features cost extra now, and could any AI features move to a paid tier later?
questions.why_it_matters: AI features often launch free or in pilot and later become paid add-ons after schools depend on them.
questions.weak_answer: No written commitment about which features stay included.

questions.question: How much staff time will this take for training, setup, and ongoing management?
questions.why_it_matters: Staff time is a real cost, and it comes out of time teachers and leaders would otherwise spend on students.
questions.weak_answer: "It's intuitive, no training needed," with no estimate of setup or support time.

questions.question: When the contract ends, can we export our data and content in a format we can actually use?
questions.why_it_matters: If you can't get your data out, switching tools later means starting over.
questions.weak_answer: Export only as PDFs, only on request, or not at all.

questions.question: How much notice do you give before raising prices or removing features, and can we exit the contract if that happens?
questions.why_it_matters: Terms that let the vendor change the product or price at any time leave you with the risk.
questions.weak_answer: Terms that allow changes without notice and no way to exit early.

questions.question: If the pilot is free, what will it cost afterward, and what happens to our data if we don't continue?
questions.why_it_matters: Free pilots can build dependence before anyone knows the real price.
questions.weak_answer: No pricing until after the pilot, or no plan for data when the pilot ends.

questions.question: Does the price depend on usage, such as per student or per AI request, and is there a cap?
questions.why_it_matters: Usage-based AI pricing can grow quickly and unpredictably as more students and teachers use the tool.
questions.weak_answer: Usage-based pricing with no cap or no way to monitor spending.

questions.question: What will a teacher actually do differently on day one, and how long will it take?
questions.why_it_matters: A clear picture of the daily workflow tells you more than a demo of what the product can do.
questions.weak_answer: A vision of transformation instead of a concrete description of what a teacher does on Monday.

questions.question: Which of our current systems does it work with, such as our student information system, learning management system, and rostering?
questions.why_it_matters: Tools that don't connect to existing systems create extra work and duplicate data entry.
questions.weak_answer: "Integrations are coming soon," or manual imports for everything.

questions.question: What does this product replace, and what does it add to teachers' work?
questions.why_it_matters: Tools that only add work tend to be abandoned, no matter how good they are.
questions.weak_answer: Nothing is replaced; the product is presented as purely additional.

questions.question: Can we talk to a district like ours that has used it for at least a year, including one that stopped using it?
questions.why_it_matters: References chosen by the vendor show the best case. A former customer shows you the risks.
questions.weak_answer: Only showcase references, and no willingness to connect you with a district that left.

questions.question: What should teachers not hand off to the AI, and how does the product make that clear?
questions.why_it_matters: Clear limits protect professional judgment and keep teachers responsible for decisions about students.
questions.weak_answer: "It can handle anything a teacher needs," with no stated limits.

questions.question: How does the product support students' thinking rather than doing the work for them?
questions.why_it_matters: A tool that produces finished work can skip the learning the assignment was meant to build.
questions.weak_answer: An emphasis on speed and polished output, with nothing about what students learn.

questions.question: How will we know in 90 days whether it's working, and what information will you give us to judge that ourselves?
questions.why_it_matters: You should be able to evaluate the tool against your goals, not only the vendor's dashboard.
questions.weak_answer: Usage dashboards only, with no connection to learning or your district's goals.

questions.question: What support is available when something breaks during the school day?
questions.why_it_matters: Problems during instruction cost class time. Response time matters.
questions.weak_answer: Email-only support with multi-day response times.
